Young announces grant funding for renovation of local park
Grants also awarded to support urban & community forestry
Rep. Regina Young
October 7, 2026 | 3:24 PM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 7
– State Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware, announced that
$145,000 has been awarded to Colwyn Borough
for the rehabilitation and development of Water Street Park. The funding was awarded through the Community Conservation Partnerships Program Grants, which are managed by the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources’ Bureau of Recreation and Conservation.
The work is expected to include renovation of basketball courts; construction of pedestrian walkways and a parking area; installation of stormwater management measures and fencing; ADA access, landscaping, a project sign, and other related site improvements.
"The folks in Colwyn deserve a modern and safe outdoor space for our young people, families, and seniors to gather, relax, and have fun," said Young. "Outdoor community spaces help us meet with our neighbors, give young folks an outlet for recreation away from a screen, and provide quiet areas for everyone to unwind and slow down. I'm so happy that Colwyn Borough will be able to move forward with these renovations for Water Street Park."
Young also pointed to two other grants awarded that will impact areas across Philadelphia:
$150,000 to the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society
to coordinate Urban and Community Forestry in the city of Philadelphia and Southeastern Pennsylvania; engage communities in planting trees and building local tree stewardship capacity in Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties.
$130,000 to the Philadelphia Department of Parks and Recreation
to coordinate and fund an Urban and Community Forestry workforce development program in the city of Philadelphia.
These
Community Conservation Partnerships Program Grants
are intended to build connections between Pennsylvanians and the outdoors by supporting recreational improvements, natural resource conservation, and community revitalization efforts.
The 185th Legislative District
is comprised of areas in South and Southwest Philadelphia, along with Tinicum Township and Colwyn Borough in Delaware County.

PA Anti-Human Trafficking Caucus, Attorney General Sunday Highlight Major Victories for Victims, Law Enforcement, Survivors
Rep. Regina Young
September 29, 2026 | 1:40 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 29 – Kicking off the fall legislative session, members of the PA Anti-Human Trafficking Caucus (AHT) today applauded two monumental legislative victories for
victims, law enforcement and survivors
.
Requested and fully supported by the Office of Attorney General,
Act 41 of 2026
(Senate Bill 45) increases criminal penalties for those who prey upon vulnerable individuals who have been groomed, manipulated and forced into “The Life.” This new law relocates most prostitution offenses to the human trafficking section of the state Crimes Code and places these offenses them under the jurisdiction of the Office of Attorney General.
“The signing of this landmark legislation proves once again that ending human trafficking takes all of us: law enforcement, prosecutors, judges, community leaders, employers, lawmakers, and especially, survivors,” said
AHT Caucus Chairman Sen. Cris Dush (R-25)
. “Specifically pertaining to Act 41, which I prime sponsored, the fundamental purpose of this new law remains and has always been giving the AG’s Office full jurisdiction to comprehensively combat prostitution and the scourge of sex trafficking across the commonwealth.”
“Combating human trafficking requires strong laws, dedicated law enforcement and an informed public. Acts 41 and 31 strengthen the work already underway at the Office of Attorney General by giving law enforcement additional tools and helping more Pennsylvanians recognize the signs of trafficking,” said
Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday
. “I commend Sen. Dush, Rep. Young and the members of the Anti-Human Trafficking Caucus for their leadership and partnership in advancing these important protections for vulnerable Pennsylvanians.”
Sponsored by
Rep. Regina G. Young (D-185)
,
Act 31 of 2026
(House Bill 1286) establishes mandatory human trafficking awareness training for Pennsylvania workers in the hospitality industry, including online lodging, reservation companies and operators of short-term rentals who have contact with guests or access to guest rooms.
“It’s crucial that we have all hands on deck in the fight to end human trafficking,” said Young. “Since hotel and other lodging staff are the folks who have the most direct contact and interaction with guests, it’s imperative that they have the training to identify the warning signs and how to report suspicious activity. Act 31 and the determination of this bipartisan, bicameral caucus are huge steps forward in helping victims escape unthinkable circumstances and putting traffickers on notice that Pennsylvania will not allow this heinous crime to continue in our commonwealth.”
Assembled earlier this spring, the mission of the PA AHT Caucus is to accelerate passage of impactful legislation through evaluating and making bipartisan and bicameral recommendations to each of the four sets of leadership in the General Assembly and the governor.
“Human trafficking is not a partisan issue,” said
Sen. Kristin Phillips-Hill (R-28)
. “I am proud of all the work done by our bipartisan, bicameral caucus, which has been able to put aside political differences to achieve real, tangible results.”
“These bills represent an important step forward in Pennsylvania’s efforts to combat human trafficking,” said
Sen. Maria Collett (D-12)
. “I’m proud to have worked alongside Senator Dush to draft and pass SB 45, now Act 41 of 2026, to strengthen the Attorney General’s ability to investigate and prosecute traffickers and sex buyers, while modernizing a legal framework that has historically placed an unfair burden on people involved in prostitution. Lawmakers examine benefits of additional school funding
Policy Committee roundtable, tour focus on Morrisville needs, outcomes
Rep. Regina Young
September 23, 2026 | 2:40 PM
MORRISVILLE, Sept. 22
–
When Pennsylvania invests in public schools that have been underfunded for years, students and communities see the difference.
Almost a year ago, Morrisville school officials warned it
could face a mid-year closure
if the state budget impasse continued. State lawmakers acted, and when the 2026-27 budget passed in July, the General Assembly provided the chronically underfunded school district with an additional $3.5 million, which will remain a permanent addition to the district’s base funding.
State Rep. Jim Prokopiak hosted the PA House Majority Policy Committee for a roundtable and tour at Morrisville on Wednesday so lawmakers could hear firsthand how the additional funds are being spent.
“When we invest in our public schools, students win and our communities win,” said Prokopiak, who represents portions of Bucks County, including Morrisville. “More dollars mean smaller school sizes and more resources for greater academic and mental health support – something that’s not possible when schools are underfunded.”
Morrisville’s experience reflects what has happened across Pennsylvania. The
Commonwealth Court found
the state’s funding system unconstitutional in 2023. Months after the ruling, the House Democratic leadership team crisscrossed the state to advocate for the
fair funding of public schools
and the most underserved school districts, making stops in Philadelphia, Berks, Centre and Allegheny counties.
Morrisville School Board president Damon Miller noted in the past, Morrisville had experienced furloughs and needed to cut programs, finding a path forward despite being underfunded and struggling financially for years.
“Having opportunities to visit smaller school districts is amazing, because it gives us an opportunity to make sure all students, all teachers and all parents are seen and heard,” said state Rep. Regina Young, who represents portions of Philadelphia and Delaware County and serves as a subcommittee chair on the House Majority Policy Committee. “All voices in this educational space should be heard and that should be a priority across the commonwealth.”
Miller added that the goal for the school now is to be more competitive with other school districts of its size when it comes to salaries. Being uncompetitive when it came to salaries led to numerous leadership changes and short-term tenures. School officials explained, the goal with additional funding is stabilization, including increasing its credit rating and exploring sustainable programs. Administrators noted that Morrisville was forced to be creative in finding answers to funding shortfalls. However, the small district has survived and remains a tight-knit district, with an estimated 850 students in the building.
“It feels like a family here, and that can’t be manufactured,” Morrisville acting interim superintendent Dr. Elaine Eib said.
Adequacy funds can be used where needed
, and across Pennsylvania, schools have used the money to hire more teachers, support technical education programs, provide mental health support, expand STEAM programming and increase staffing.
“We’re seeing what happens when resources reach the students who need them,” said state Rep. Ryan Bizzarro, who represents portions of Erie County and serves as the House Majority Policy Committee chairman. “The progress in Morrisville shows why sustained investment matters. We need to keep closing the gaps, so every student has an opportunity to succeed, regardless of their ZIP code.”
The committee was joined by interim acting school superintendent
Dr. Elaine Eib
, business manager Dea Popovski, middle/senior high school principal Brian Oberdick, elementary (K-5) principal Nick Zlupko, and school board president Damon Miller.
Information about this hearing and other House Majority Policy Committee hearings can be found at
pahouse.com/policy
. Photos to be used for publication can be found on the day of the hearing at
Facebook.com/PADemPolic

Young announces over $1M in funding for area projects
Rep. Regina Young
September 16, 2026 | 11:40 AM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 16
–
State Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware
, announced that four projects in her legislative district have been awarded state funding for a total of $1,071,224. The funds were awarded by the
Commonwealth Financing Authority
through the
Local Share Account
, which distributes money for eligible community and economic development projects from state gaming revenues.
Two projects are located in the South and Southwest Philadelphia areas of the 185th Legislative District:
$250,000 for police station renovations at the Philadelphia International Airport.
$150,000 for Sharing Excess to purchase vehicles to help distribute donated food to local food banks and compost to local ag programs and gardens.
Two projects are located in the Delaware County areas of the 185th Legislative District:
$463,250 for renovations and modernization for Colwyn Borough Hall.
$207,974 for the Tinicum Township Police Department to purchase and upfit three police vehicles.
“This funding will go directly into improving public safety and access for our communities, which is a great use of LSA monies,” said Young. “Our Delaware County public infrastructure has been in real need of modernizing, so the continued renovations of Colwyn Borough Hall and improved ability for timely response by Tinicum Township police is long overdue and welcome. I’m also thrilled to support public safety improvements at the airport and assist Sharing Excess with obtaining new vehicles to help with their mission to improve food insecurity in Philadelphia and Delco. LSA funds should be used for uplifting quality of life and the public interest. These investments show how we can do so much more when we work together.”
For more on the LSA program, visit:
dced.pa.gov/programs/local-share-account-lsa-statewide
.
The 185th Legislative District
is comprised of areas in South and Southwest Philadelphia, along with Tinicum Township and Colwyn Borough in Delaware County.

Lawmakers examine service, needs of river pilots
Policy Committee joined by Pilots’ Association for roundtable, tour
Rep. Regina Young
September 8, 2026 | 4:34 PM
PHILADELPHIA, Sept. 8 –
Keeping commerce and trade open 24/7 comes with its challenges and obstacles, including preserving domestic security as well as navigating waterways through challenging weather. The
Pilots’ Association for the Bay & River Delaware
are on call at all hours to ensure the safe navigation of commercial vessels along the Delaware, Schuylkill and Salem rivers as well as Delaware Bay.
“The Pilots’ Association helps keep us safe, and river pilots keep Pennsylvania open for business,” said state Rep. Mary Isaacson, who represents portions of Philadelphia and serves as the Policy Committee Vice Chair. “They do it all despite the job’s rigorous demands, which include obtaining years of training and valuable experience.”
State lawmakers met with the Pilots’ Association during a roundtable and tour along the Delaware River, seeing the operation firsthand.
“There’s no room for error for river pilots, navigating waterways during storms, icy conditions and dense fog,” said Rep. Regina Young, who represents portions of Philadelphia. “Business never stops, and these workers deserve credit for keeping our bridges safe as they pilot massive container vessels.”
Among the legislation discussed during the roundtable, officials noted
Rep. Anthony Bellmon
’s
H.B. 2426
, which would increase the draft size of vessels to 29 feet – easing unnecessary restrictions on river pilots and keep them competitive.
“It’s easy to overlook the work of river pilots, because when the job is done correctly everything runs smoothly,” said Policy Committee Chairman and state Rep. Ryan Bizzarro, who represents portions of Erie County. “However, traveling the Delaware River this afternoon, and seeing just one of the massive container vessels reveals just how vital their work can be. They keep us safe, and they keep goods headed to our communities.”
Founded in 1896, the organization is one of the oldest state pilot organizations in the nation and a world leader in technology, training and accountability. The organization consists of 67 pilots from Pennsylvania and Delaware. Pilots typically have extensive maritime experience and train for three or more years before being issued state and federal licenses. Following 9/11, pilots became an even more critical component in protecting and providing security at U.S. ports.
Massive vessels along the river can contain as many as 16,000 containers, headed for rail and truck transit. Some of the largest container vessels only have 2-3 feet of clearance on the river, so river pilots are tasked with captaining the ship at high tide to maintain safe passage.
Lawmakers participated in a roundtable with Pilots’ Association President Capt. David K. Cuff in the association’s south Philadelphia office before Cuff took lawmakers on a boat traveling along the Delaware River to view the Packer Avenue Marine Terminal, which is located south of the Walt Whitman Bridge, and the Hanwha Philly Shipyard.

Young presents major grant funding for projects at Bartram’s Garden
Rep. Regina Young
August 12, 2026 | 1:33 PM
PHILADELPHIA, Aug. 12
– Today,
state Rep. Regina Young
, D-Phila./Delaware, presented a check for a $1 million grant from Pennsylvania’s Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program to
Bartram’s Garden
for several projects on their campus.
The grant will support the construction of the Ecosystems Education Center at Bartram's Garden, reconfiguration of the main driveway to Bartram's Garden and the Bartram's Mile Trail to include a pedestrian sidewalk and designated bike lane for safe multi-modal traffic, and restoration of the pedestrian bridge connecting Bartram’s Village.
“Bartram’s Garden is a wonderful oasis in our southwest Philadelphia backyard, and I’m proud to advocate for more resources to help develop and maintain this educational campus,” said Young. “These projects will expand mobility around the facility and reconnect the grounds with the Bartram Village public housing complex so that everyone can access and enjoy the possibilities available across the gardens. From educational opportunity to the public gardens, to the riverfront access, there is something for everyone at Bartram’s Garden, with so much more to come!”
Young presented the check to Maitreyi Roy, executive director at Bartram's Garden, who expressed appreciation for the state’s support of their mission.
“This investment brings us one step closer to breaking ground on the Ecosystems Education Center and creating a place where young people, families, and neighbors can learn directly from the living systems that surround them,” said Roy. “We are deeply grateful to state Sen. Anthony Williams and Rep. Regina Young for their leadership and belief in this vision. As we move toward construction, this support builds real momentum for a project that will inspire environmental stewardship and serve the Southwest Philadelphia community for generations.”
The Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program
is a state grant program administered by the Office of the Budget for the design, acquisition and construction of regional economic, cultural, civic, recreational and historical improvement projects. RACP projects are authorized in the Redevelopment Assistance section of a Capital Budget Itemization Act, have a regional or multi-jurisdictional impact, and generate substantial increases or maintain levels of employment, tax revenues or other measures of economic activity. Projects under RACP cannot obtain primary funding under other state programs.

Delaware County legislators’ statement on threats to Sheriff Kamara
Rep. Regina Young
July 30, 2026 | 2:11 PM
UPPER DARBY, July 29 –
The Delaware County House Delegation today released the following statement on the race-based threats received by Delaware County Sheriff Siddiq Kamara:
“The Delaware County House Delegation unequivocally condemns the recent terroristic threats directed at Delaware County Sheriff Siddiq Kamara. There is no place for intimidation, violence or hate against those who choose to serve and live in any community in our county and the state.
“Public servants regardless of political party, position or ideology should never be subjected to threats of violence for carrying out their sworn responsibilities, or for their faith, background or culture. An attack or threat against one public official is an attack on the principles of democracy, public service and the rule of law that bind our Commonwealth together.
“As members of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, we stand in unwavering solidarity with Sheriff Kamara, his family and the dedicated professionals of the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office. We also stand with Delaware County's diverse communities, including our vibrant immigrant communities, who deserve to live free from fear, hate and intimidation. Now that an arrest has been made, those responsible for these terroristic threats must be held fully accountable and a clear precedent must be set that such acts of intimidation and violence against public servants will not be tolerated.
“The safety of our elected officials, law enforcement officers, public employees and every resident is paramount. We refuse to accept a climate where threats and fear are used to silence, intimidate or undermine those who serve the public. Violence and hate have no place in Delaware County or anywhere across the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
“We call on all Pennsylvanians to reject rhetoric that fuels division and instead embrace civility, respect and the peaceful exchange of ideas. While we may disagree on issues and policies, there is never a justification for threats of violence or acts of terror.
“The Delaware County House Delegation remains steadfast in its commitment to protecting our communities and supporting those who dedicate their lives to public service. We will continue to stand united against violence, hate and intimidation, and we reaffirm that acts of terroristic threats against public servants or anyone in our communities must be met with swift justice and the full force of the law.”

Gov. Shapiro signs Young’s anti-human trafficking bill into law
New law will help combat human trafficking in PA by requiring training for hospitality workers
Rep. Regina Young
July 20, 2026
HARRISBURG, July 20
–
A state House bill
designed to help combat human trafficking in Pennsylvania was signed into law today by Gov. Josh Shapiro. Authored by
state Rep. Regina Young
, D-Phila./Delaware, the law, Act 31 of 2026, mandates human trafficking awareness training for Pennsylvania workers in the hospitality industry, including online lodging and reservation companies.
Among other provisions, the law includes training requirements approved through the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency for employees of public lodging establishments who have contact with guests or access to guest rooms, and for operators of short-term rentals.
Young said this legislation, the first of its kind in Pennsylvania pertaining to human trafficking, is borne from the reality that her region is a prime location for traffickers.
“With our proximity to major interstate highways and international transportation hubs, South Philadelphia and Delaware County are unfortunate hotbeds for this evil practice, though the problem continues to be pervasive across the state,” said Young.
“This law will give front desk and housekeeping staff training to identify signs of human trafficking and what they can do to report it. These staff are some of the most engaged employees with guests, so they should be educated to recognize and report suspected trafficking. It also encompasses online reservation services to account for their specific set of warning signs as a popular and easy option to bypass face-to-face interaction,” added Young. “It’s not just hotels and motels – it’s also inclusive of short-term rental operators.”
Young said given the number of national and international events happening in Pennsylvania, it was important to bring this issue into the light and continue to take steps to address it.
In October, the House Tourism, Recreation & Economic Development Committee
held a public hearing
on the legislation in Delaware County which outlined the critical need for this reform as sexual exploitation is a pervasive and ongoing problem. Expert testimony laid out the case for Pennsylvania to do more in its fight against human trafficking.
“I want to thank all of my colleagues, on both sides of the aisle and in the Senate, for heeding the experts who sounded the alarm on this issue, and for their support of my bill,” Young said. “We have much more work to do on this issue, but this is a great step to providing people with the tools they need to help others who may be trapped in horrible circumstances.”

Young announces major grant funding for area projects
Rep. Regina Young
July 16, 2026
PHILADELPHIA, July 16
– State Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware, announced today that six projects in her legislative district have been awarded grants totaling $10.2 million from Pennsylvania’s Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program.
The projects are all located in the South and Southwest Philadelphia sections of the 185th Legislative District:
$500,000 to Bartram Village for site preparation for affordable housing.
$1 million to Bartram's Garden Campus for construction of the Ecosystems Education Center at Bartram's Garden, reconfiguring the main driveway and restoring a pedestrian bridge.
$350,000 to FloatLab IX and Philadelphia Mural Arts for the final phase of construction for FloatLab at Bartram’s Garden.
$350,000 to GPHA Medical and Behavioral Health Campus for development of a comprehensive medical campus.
$4 million to the Philadelphia Eagles Training Facility to expand, develop and construct several integral parts of the facility.
$4 million to Rhoads Industries Building to construct a new waterfront building.
“These projects mean so much to our community, so I’m proud to be able to support these investments in our cultural well-being, health and safety, plus job creation and innovation,” Young said. “This is one of the most important parts of my job in state government and delivering for Philadelphia and Delaware counties.”
Young also pointed to a major grant awarded to Riddle Memorial Hospital in Media, Delaware County, that will help it update its emergency room facilities and infrastructure and ensure it remains part of the health care options for area residents.
“In Delaware County, we need to support all the health care resources we still have, as we’ve seen so many hospital and health facility closures in recent years,” Young said. “This impressive investment in Riddle Hospital should help ensure that their emergency facilities contain state-of-the-art equipment and the necessary infrastructure to remain a vital part of health care solutions for our communities without having to travel great distances to Philadelphia or beyond.”
RACP is a state grant program administered by the Office of the Budget for the design, acquisition and construction of regional economic, cultural, civic, recreational and historical improvement projects.
RACP projects are authorized in the Redevelopment Assistance section of a Capital Budget Itemization Act, have a regional or multi-jurisdictional impact, and generate substantial increases or maintain levels of employment, tax revenues or other measures of economic activity. Projects under RACP cannot obtain primary funding under other state programs. More information about the program is available at
https://www.pa.gov/agencies/budget/programs-and-services/for-people-doing-business-with-the-commonwealth/for-grantees-and-subrecipients/racp

Rep. Regina Young

HARRISBURG, July 12
– Legislation sponsored by state Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware, to mandate human-trafficking awareness training for Pennsylvania workers in the hospitality industry, including for online lodging and reservation companies, is set to become law having gained final approval in the state House and Senate today.
“I’m so proud to have this vision finally get to the governor’s desk,” Young said. “I’ve been working on this concept with my legislative colleagues in the PA Anti-Human Trafficking Caucus, Philadelphia City Council, and the lodging industry for several years to develop an agreeable plan for everyone, so this is a long time coming.

House Bill 1286
has overwhelming industry support and was unanimously approved in the House. Governor Josh Shapiro has 10 days to sign the bill into law.
The 185th Legislative District is comprised of areas in South and Southwest Philadelphia, along with Tinicum Township and Colwyn Borough in Delaware County.

PHILADELPHIA, May 29

House Appropriations
Chairman Jordan Harris, D-Phila., and state Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware, hosted a Community Budget Briefing Thursday alongside the Philadelphia House Delegation.
Harris and Young hosted the briefing for Philadelphians to learn about the budget process, understand how state funding decisions impact their communities, and voice their opinions on what should be included in the state budget.

Letter to PUC chair cites ‘significant financial hardships’ on ratepayers

Members of the Pennsylvania House Democratic Southeast Delegation today wrote to the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission to express their strong opposition to proposed gas and electric rate hikes by PECO, according to state Rep. Jennifer O’Mara, D-Delaware, the delegation chair.

The Democratic Southeast Delegation includes House members from Bucks, Chester, Delaware and Montgomery counties.
In addition to urging the PUC to reject the rate increases, the delegation members asked the commission to hold four public hearings on the proposals, one in each of Philadelphia’s collar counties.
“Holding local hearings will allow for greater accessibility and transparency for our constituents, who deserve to be a part of this process,” the legislators wrote.

House Majority Policy Committee examine ideas to help more seniors afford prescription medications
Legislation would raise income limits for PA’s prescription assistance programs
Rep. Regina Young
March 10, 2026 | 1:03 PM
HARRISBURG, March 10 –
As costs continue to rise on everything, including prescription drug prices, many seniors are being forced to make impossible decisions. The House Majority Policy Committee convened a hearing Tuesday, hosted by Rep. Regina Young (D-Phila./Delaware), to discuss what can be done to help more seniors afford their medications.
“No one who spent a lifetime working and contributing to their community should have to decide between filling a prescription and buying groceries. Access to affordable prescription medication isn’t a luxury, it’s a necessity for staying healthy and living with dignity,” Young said. “We have to continue working to lower costs and make sure seniors can afford the medications they rely on, without having to sacrifice the other basic needs of daily life.”
A livestream of Tuesday’s hearing is
available here
.
PACE and PACENET, Pennsylvania’s prescription assistance programs that offer low-cost prescription medication to eligible seniors, currently serve more than 250,000 older Pennsylvanians. Earlier this session, the General Assembly passed an extension of the Social Security COLA moratorium for these programs, allowing enrollees to remain eligible for the program if their Social Security COLA exceeds the income eligibility limit. This extension allowed more than 22,000 PACE and PACENET enrollees to keep their coverage and low co-payments.
House Democrats are committed to continue helping older Pennsylvanians. Young has introduced
legislation
that would allow even more seniors to qualify for PACE and PACENET by raising the income eligibility requirements for the program. Under the proposal, the income limit cap would be raised to $45,000 for a single person and $55,000 for a couple.
Testifiers at Tuesday’s hearing included two Pennsylvania seniors struggling to afford their prescription medications who spoke in favor of the legislation. It also featured testimony from Roy Afflerbach, Government Relations Specialist for the
Pennsylvania Association for Area Agencies on Aging
.
“At a time when costs are rising across the board, we have to be focused on the everyday expenses that impact people the most. For many seniors, that starts with the price of prescription medications, and keeping those costs low remains a priority of the House Democratic Caucus,” said House Majority Policy Chairman Ryan Bizzarro D-Erie). “We will continue to identify solutions that lower costs and make life a little easier for the seniors who depend on these medications every day.”

Awards will strengthen FDR Park ecology and trails
Rep. Regina Young
February 11, 2026 | 11:50 AM
PHILADELPHIA, Feb. 11 – State Rep. Regina Young
, D-Phila./Delaware, joined leaders from the Fairmount Park Conservancy and Philadelphia Parks & Recreation to announce $275,000 in newly awarded state grants for improvement projects at historic FDR Park in South Philadelphia.
Funding through the CFA
Greenways, Trails, and Recreation Program
:
$125,000 to Fairmount Park Conservancy for the FDR Park Nature Phase Franklin 5K to connect all the landscapes in the park for cyclists and pedestrians, allowing for safer travel and exploration from the plaza to the park's natural lands and beyond.
Funding through the PA
Watershed Restoration Protection Program
:
$150,000 for ecological restoration along Shedbrook Creek to bring stronger ecology, thousands of climate-resilient trees, and biodiverse native plants to FDR Park.
Photo: Erin Blewett for Fairmount Park Conservancy
Young said that she was happy to advocate for these grants to support the FDR Park Plan and develop open, green, recreational and education spaces for children and families.
“FDR Park, by design, has been a community resource for recreation and nature for over 100 years. There are immense public benefits of both, especially for children,” said Young.
“We cannot say the word ‘park’ without thinking of children, which is why we must continue creating spaces for our youth in Philadelphia. At a time when so many young people are facing challenges related to mental health and access to safe physical spaces, we must work together to support their overall well-being. These grants will help foster growth and opportunity within FDR Park for all of our young people. Together, we can accomplish so much more.”
Photo: Erin Blewett for Fairmount Park Conservancy
Tony Sorrentino
, CEO of Fairmount Park Conservancy, said the impacts of the restoration projects in FDR Park are immense for access to nature, improved public health, and recreational access for children and families.
“The state investments we’re celebrating today, which are restoring these natural elements, demonstrate a renewed commitment to two of the park’s greatest strengths: accessibility and its extraordinary natural history. It’s very rare to find that combination in any city across the country, and we have it all right here at Broad and Pattison. These projects reflect our commitment to the vision for what these 348 acres will mean to Philadelphia,” Sorrentino said.
Photo: Erin Blewett for Fairmount Park Conservancy
Philadelphia Parks & Recreation commissioner
Susan Slawson
said the investments are already paying off with wetland restoration and the return of wildlife to the park.
“This is a step forward for FDR Park, Fairmount Park Conservancy, and the city of Philadelphia,” said Slawson.
“FDR Park is truly one of a kind, with lakes, creeks and wetlands — you won’t find another park like it anywhere else in Philadelphia. We want to ensure that Philadelphia is a premier city for everyone.”
The FDR Park Plan represents Philadelphia’s largest and most public-facing collaborative investment in climate resilience, expanding equitable and diverse access for residents across the city as the park enters its second century.

Speaker of the House Joanna McClinton

“Over the past three years, we’ve steered historic resources to districts like William Penn because strong communities begin with strong schools,” McClinton said. “Every student deserves access to the learning tools they need to succeed.

“William Penn didn’t just expose an unconstitutional funding system; it forced the Commonwealth to fix it,” said
state Rep. Jordan Harris, D-Phila.,
majority chairman of the House Appropriations Committee. “Now we must make sure those commitments show up in the budget year after year, so students see real changes in their schools -- from classroom stability to spaces that support their growth and success.”

Young announces over $2.9M in state funding for local infrastructure projects
Rep. Regina Young
January 21, 2026 | 4:08 PM
HARRISBURG, Jan. 21
– State Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware, announced that $2.9 million has been awarded by the
Commonwealth Financing Authority
to local transportation and sewer projects to improve public safety and quality of life in the 185th Legislative District.
Three projects were awarded funding through the state’s
Multimodal Transportation Fund
to support local transportation projects that encourage economic development and safe transit:
$1.3 million to Philadelphia Authority for Industrial Development for roadway realignment and improvements to pedestrian and bicyclist safety along South Broad Street at the Navy Yard.
$750,000 to the City of Philadelphia Department of Aviation to replace signage at the Philadelphia International Airport.
$433,000 to Schuylkill River Development Corporation for pedestrian and bicyclist safety improvements at the intersection of Passyunk Avenue and 61st Street.
One project was awarded funding from the state’s
Small Water and Sewer Program
, which provides grants to communities for water, sewer, storm water, and flood control projects:
$425,000 to Colwyn Borough for Pine Street sanitary sewer improvements.
“These investments will go a long way to improving the safety of pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers in our communities, as well as protecting public health with sewer improvements in Colwyn,” said Young. “I’m thankful for the continued importance the Shapiro administration places on improving the everyday lives of people in South and Southwest Philadelphia and Delaware County.”
Funding for both programs is administered by the Commonwealth Financing Authority, an independent agency established in 2004 to manage Pennsylvania’s economic stimulus initiatives.
The 185th Legislative District is comprised of areas in South and Southwest Philadelphia, along with Tinicum Township and Colwyn Borough in Delaware County.

Young Announces $2.1 million in investments for community projects and infrastructure
Eleven Awards Announced Across Multiple CFA Funding Programs
Rep. Regina Young
December 19, 2025
HARRISBURG, Dec. 19 –
State Rep. Regina Young
, D-Phila./Delaware, on Thursday announced more than $2.1 million in state funding for community projects and infrastructure improvements in the 185th Legislative District, awarded through the
Commonwealth Financing Authority
.
A total of more than $1.4 million in Local Share Account funding will support the following projects:
$350,000 to the Philadelphia City Department of Aviation for structural repairs -- including concrete work, waterproofing, and expansion joint replacement -- on floors 1 through 5 of Parking Garage C at Philadelphia International Airport.
$200,000 to People Advancing Reintegration Inc. for a building acquisition project aimed at reducing recidivism and supporting individuals returning to society after incarceration.
$250,000 to the American Swedish Historical Foundation to construct a lighted, drive-up, fully accessible entrance and parking area for the museum, along with new stormwater infrastructure and site fencing.
$150,000 to Sharing Excess Inc. to purchase a refrigeration box truck and van for use in Philadelphia.
$163,475 to The Friends of FDR Park to enhance transportation and mobility with the addition of a 40-passenger ADA-accessible electric tram, a passenger van, and a skid steer.
$300,000 to Colwyn Borough (Delaware County) for improvements to the borough hall, creating a modern community space for meetings, educational programs, and recreational events.
Young also highlighted nearly $300,000 in LSA investments for Delaware County projects, including Flood/Stream Gauges ($224,274) and a Teachers' Teammates Delivery Van ($67,943).
Two projects received funding through the CFA Greenways, Trails, and Recreation Program:
$145,000 to Colwyn Borough for Water Street Park basketball court renovations.
$125,000 to Fairmount Park Conservancy for the FDR Park Nature Phase Franklin 5K.
Additionally, the Watershed Restoration Protection Program awarded $150,000 to Fairmount Park Conservancy to fund the Shedbrook Creek Riparian Restoration.
“We are so fortunate in the 185th to receive these funds from the Commonwealth Financing Authority,” said Young. “These investments are a lifeline for community assets and organizations that do incredible work in our neighborhoods, while also improving infrastructure that keeps our communities healthy, clean, and safe in South and Southwest Philadelphia and Delaware County.”
The PA Race Horse Development and Gaming Act distributes gaming revenues through the Commonwealth Financing Authority to support projects in the public interest across Pennsylvania.
Eligible projects include acquisition, construction, renovation, and rehabilitation; demolition; infrastructure improvements; purchase of vehicles, machinery, and equipment; planning, consulting, and design costs; engineering; and certain administrative expenses.

Young introduces legislation to combat bullying in nonpublic schools
The Jack Reid Law would be similar to NY law that honors life of 17-year-old
Rep. Regina Young
October 14, 2026 | 3:09 PM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 14
– State Rep. Regina Young, D-Phila./Delaware, has introduced legislation designed to protect students in Pennsylvania nonpublic schools from bullying.
The “Jack Reid Law” was enacted in New York state in October 2025 to extend anti-bullying protections to students attending nonpublic schools, ensuring that all students have access to a safe learning environment regardless of where they attend school. The law is named in memory of Jack Reid, a 17-year-old student whose life was tragically cut short after enduring persistent bullying at a private school.
“I was proud to vote for our 2026-27 state budget that strengthens anti-bullying laws in public schools, but we can’t ignore the safety of students in private and parochial schools,” said Young. “Students spend most of their day in school, and as a parent myself, I know the worry of kids being safe while they’re away from home. This bill would provide parents and students the peace of mind of these protections while they’re in school no matter where they attend classes.”
More than 250,000 students attend nonpublic schools in Pennsylvania and do not receive the same statutory protection against bullying as students in public schools.
House Bill 2816
would require nonpublic schools to:
adopt and periodically review their policies related to bullying, and review the policy with the school community.
make the policy publicly accessible on the school’s internet website, if available, and in every classroom.
post the policy prominently throughout school buildings.
promptly investigate alleged incidents of bullying.
notify the students involved in alleged incidents of bullying.
promptly notify the students and parents who were involved in the alleged bullying of the outcome of the investigation.
As a former educator and current member of the House Education Committee, Young recently met with Elizabeth and Bill Reid, the parents of Jack Reid, to discuss the New York law and how it can be implemented in Pennsylvania.
“I’m working to ensure that all Pennsylvania students are afforded the same basic protection from bullying and have the opportunity to learn in a safe and supportive environment. Meeting with the Reids who are turning their unimaginable loss and experience into a positive for families across the nation was an impactful, emotional, and productive discussion. Through their
Jack Reid Foundation
, they are ensuring that no parents will have to endure the tragedy of losing a child as the result of bullying.”
The bill has been referred to the
House Education Committee
for consideration.
